subject: Staging->Prod IaC safety review for private deployment
messages:
From: Ethan Park <ethan@atlasdata.com>

Cc: OnPremOps <ops@onpremops.io>
Date: Tue, 25 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Staging->Prod IaC runway: private deploy safety review

Hi Jordan —

Thanks again for taking this on. We're planning to promote our private deployment bundle from staging to prod next week for the AtlasData customer site in the us-west cluster. Before we flip traffic, legal/security asked for a short, focused IaC safety review that covers networking, secrets/KMS handling, and CI gating.

What I attached:
- tf-plan-staging.diff (staging plan with drift)
- helm-values-prod.yaml (proposed prod overrides)
- ansible-playbook-runbook.md (playbook we run as part of the rollout)

Key asks:
- Quick read on any missing network restrictions (NACLs, subnet tagging) that could expose management ports.
- Confirm KMS key usage in TF and that secrets aren't leaked to build logs.
- Validation steps for Prometheus/healthcheck changes in helm values.

Can we get a 30–45 minute review call and a short checklist of gating items? OnPremOps is available to run a dry-run on 2026-08-29 between 09:00–12:00 PDT if that works for your team.

Cheers,
Ethan
Ethan Park | Platform Engineer, AtlasData

Subject: Re: Staging->Prod IaC runway: private deploy safety review

Ethan —

Thanks for the materials. We can run the 30–45m review and produce a short gating checklist. Proposed plan:

1) Pre-review (today): quick scan of the TF plan + helm values (Irene will take TF; Rishi will look at the helm + runtime observability changes).
2) Review call (2026-08-28, 10:00 PDT) — 30m to cover findings and sign-off items.
3) Dry-run (OnPremOps) on 2026-08-29 in the 09:00–12:00 PDT window.
4) Post-dry-run: we expect a short runbook update and a PR to the prod overrides branch.

Initial notes from my quick pass:
- Add a CI gate that fails on any public-ip creation in private subnets unless explicitly approved.
- Verify KMS key policy referenced in the TF module: we need key rotation annotation and no broad principals.
- Helm: ensure readinessProbe thresholds are conservative for the first 24h after cutover to avoid mass restarts.

I'll attach a short checklist PDF (priv-deploy-safety-checklist.pdf) and link to a runbook page. Irene/Rishi — flag anything urgent below and we'll cover it in the call.

Jordan Blake | Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

On Wed, Aug 26, 2026 at 11:03 AM Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com> wrote:
> Initial notes from my quick pass:
> - Add a CI gate that fails on any public-ip creation in private subnets unless explicitly approved.
> - Verify KMS key policy referenced in the TF module: we need key rotation annotation and no broad principals.
> - Helm: ensure readinessProbe thresholds are conservative for the first 24h after cutover to avoid mass restarts.

Thanks — I pulled the TF plan and did a focused sweep. High-level findings:

1) Networking
- I see two places in the module where an elastic IP is conditionally created based on var.expose_mgmt (default: false). The plan shows it as created (staging drift). We should make that var immutable in the prod branch or require an explicit approval tag.
- Missing NACL deny rule for 2379-2380 (etcd ports) across one private subnet (subnet-id: subnet-0a12). Recommend adding a TF test that asserts NACL blocks inbound 0.0.0.0/0 on management ports.

2) Secrets/KMS
- KMS usage is present but the key_policy allows aws:PrincipalOrgID from a wildcarded org principal — bit too broad. Patch to tighten to redwood-admin-role and the atlas-service-role only.
- Looked for any echoing of secrets into user_data / render templates. There are two templated systemd units that write a token; ensure those use vault-agent templating rather than plain interpolation.

3) CI/CD gates and runbook
- Add a terratest job that runs terraform plan --diff and fails on any network resource with public_ip.
- The ansible playbook includes a step that restarts the model-serving process without healthcheck gating. Add a canary flag and a pause-check command.

Patch suggestion: I prepared tf-module-proposed-patches.diff with the NACL assertion and tightened KMS policy (attached). Also left inline comments for helm-values-prod.yaml to lower liveness aggressiveness for 24h.

I'll be on the review call and can walk the TF diff.

Irene Choi | Staff Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference

Really helpful — thanks for the quick turnaround and the patches. OnPremOps will run the dry-run in the 09:00–12:00 PDT window today and report back with a plan/rollback estimate. Two quick confirmations from our side before we proceed:

- We will tag the prod branch with "manual-approval: true" for any EIP/public-ip changes and the terratest gate will catch accidental drift.
- AtlasData security will validate the tightened KMS policy tonight.

I'll share the dry-run logs and a short summary (expected downtime: none; potential risk: brief readiness flaps) in this thread when complete. If the run proves clean, can we get a final sign-off from Jordan and Irene to merge the prod overrides PR?
